result.topic_en: Ramanujan determines the asymptotic order of the numbers x_r in his theory of highly composite (generalised) numbers, the largest exponent a_2, the expansion of log N, and estimates for the products Π_r(x) in terms of zeta values.
result.transcription:
69. We shall consider the order of $x_r$. Putting $r=1$ in (319) we have
$\epsilon = \frac{\log(1+x_1^{-s})}{\log x_1}$;
and so
(364) $x_r^{\frac{\log(1+x_1^{-s})}{\log x_1}} = \frac{1-x_r^{-s(r+1)}}{1-x_r^{-sr}}$.
Let $x_r = x_1^{t_r/r}$.
Then we have
$(1+x_1^{-s})^{t_r/r} = \frac{1-x_1^{-st_r(1+\frac{1}{r})}}{1-x_1^{-st_r}}$
From this we can easily deduce that
$t_r = 1 + \frac{\log r}{s\log x_1} + O\left\{\frac{1}{(\log x_1)^2}\right\}$.
Hence
(365) $x_r = x_1^{1/r}\left\{r^{1/(rs)} + O\left(\frac{1}{\log x_1}\right)\right\}$;
and so
(366) $x_r \sim (r^{1/s}x_1)^{1/r}$.
